prompt:
I need the front end for Framestate Locations. The location search system of a state film office, used by its staff to find public and private properties available for filming and send candidates to production companies considering shooting in the state.

Who's using it: Desmond Achebe, a production services coordinator at the state film office. He's a former location scout, now a state employee, and he handles incoming requests from out-of-state productions deciding whether to film there. He knows the location library well but not every one of its thousands of properties.

What they're doing right now: A mid-budget streaming series sent a scouting request this morning: a 1970s-style small-town courthouse interior with a balcony gallery, a main street that can be closed for two nights, and a disused rail yard, all within 90 minutes' drive of the capital so the crew can stay in one hotel. The production's location manager wants a first set of candidates by end of day. Desmond is describing each need in his own words, narrowing by drive time, permit history and owner willingness, and comparing what comes back. He also wants to see properties similar to a courthouse he already likes but can't use because it's under renovation until spring.

What's in the system at this point: About 4,200 registered locations, each with name, county, property type, owner type (state, municipal, private), era and architectural style tags, 8–60 reference photos, square footage, ceiling height, power access, parking capacity, drive time from the capital, past productions filmed there (e.g. 'Hollow County' S2, 2023), permit lead time, any blackout dates, and owner-contact status (active, unresponsive, declined filming). 37 courthouses statewide, 11 of them with balconies. 140 main-street segments with closure rules set by each city. 9 rail yards, 3 owned by the state DOT. Today's request is logged as SR-2026-0418 with three needs, a shoot window of March 9–April 24, 2027, and a 25-person crew size.

Build it as a working web app, opened in the state that person would see at that moment. No backend: use realistic mock data (no lorem ipsum, no placeholder names), and make the interactive parts actually work client-side.

Use whatever framework and tooling you like. When you're done there must be a static production build in ./out with ./out/index.html as the entry point. It will be served from the root of a plain static file server (no rewrites, no server code) and viewed in a desktop browser at 1440×900.
